patches.notes: First patch through the launcher: proves the auto-updater works. Patches download by themselves from here on.

Roads: all 1,370 km of the Tweed's real roads (OpenStreetMap), cut and filled into the terrain. Cracked old bitumen, faded line markings, gravel shoulders, kerbs and footpaths in town, dirt farm tracks, bridges with barriers and piers, grass and moss creeping back in. Creative / survival mode (Esc menu): Forge only in creative. Forge gets Weapons, Car parts, Tools, Survival, World and Nature tabs with ~100 new Poly Haven scans plus four engines (Holden 202, Toyota 22R, Ford 351 Cleveland, Jeep 4.0) with bolt-on alternators. Cars and props left far away no longer fall through the world.
Updater upgrade: lets the launcher download big updates in pieces. If the next update shows a download error, close the game and open it again.
Updater fix: no time limit on big downloads.

Big one. Simulated driving: real engine torque curves, auto and manual boxes, clutch, diffs (open / LSD / locked), raycast suspension with springs, dampers, bump stops and sway bars, Pacejka tyres; you can watch the shocks, springs, leaf packs, wishbones and sway bars work under the car. Engine sounds synthesised for the 202, 22R, 351 Cleveland and Jeep 4.0, with crackle on lift-off and the starter. Zombies (slow, arms out, they hit hard) and scavs (patrol, suspicion, whistle alarm, they shoot back). Ragdolls, limbs and heads come off, blood, run them over. Six period guns (Lee-Enfield, SLR, Colt Python, side-by-side, sawn-off, 870 pump) held in your hands, aim down the sights with right mouse. Garage (Esc menu, creative): build a vehicle from any cab on a ladder chassis, pick engine, box, axles, springs, travel, damping, tyres, add a third axle, save and drive it. Scanned grass up close. Credits page.

Animation overhaul: every character now shares one humanoid skeleton, so 50+ clips play on any body. New rifle animations (idle, walk, run, crouch, reload), body turns to follow where you look after ~70 degrees (35 with a gun up), head and spine look where the camera looks, legs swing toward the way you're walking. Hands properly on the gun in first and third person (right hand on the grip, left under the fore-end). Scopes on the Lee-Enfield (3.5x) and SLR (4x): aim to get a magnified scope window. Five new zombie models with real zombie walks, idles, attacks, bites and a scream when they spot you. 14 scav camps across the map (fire, shelters, barricades, a wreck, loot, a sentry on the gate). Zombies now wander in along the roads, out of sight, instead of fixed spawns.

F9 bug report: grabs a screenshot and the whole game state (where you are, what you're driving or holding, nearby zombies and scavs, settings, frame rate, recent log), pauses, and lets you type what happened. Save it as a zip, or Send it straight to a private GitHub repo for Claude to read.
Fix: keys added in updates (F9 bug report, fire, aim, reload, weapon slots, holster) weren't being registered on installed copies. They are now.
F9 bug report box now sits in the middle of the screen, so the Send button and token box are visible.

Inventory (I): Unturned-style grid with shaped items, worn clothes and bags add pockets, guns load from carried rounds; F opens crates, ammo boxes and other props; MMB carry, RMB throw; B bandage. HUD health and ammo fixed. New PBR ground at real scale, BlendKit lawn, Poly Haven grass clumps everywhere. Water ripple grid fixed. Iron sights measured from each gun (no more rifles in your face), revolver turned the right way round. Mid-air leg pose. Zombies quieter, no more floor-eating attack. Tyres: grip by ground type, slide falloff, tyre pressure, deflection, smoke, rubber marks, screech, dirt spray; Globe mags in the garage. Cars no longer get stuck on corpses.

Roads round the pub and down Tweed Valley Way past the gallery rebuilt with a node road generator from real map data: proper roundabout with a kerbed island, junctions, and the overtaking lane south of the gallery. Inventory items now have pictures that fill their grid shape (rifles long, pistols short). Engine sounds re-recorded from a real engine simulator. Less blue tint on roads and pale ground; matte ground textures.
Fixes the crash on Play from 0.2.11 (a road texture was missing from the build). The game now also starts without the new roads if they ever fail to load.

Zombies now move on the Hollow Walker's animations: walkers that break into a run when close, shamblers with an unsteady drag, and lurchers that charge head-down; they scream when they spot you. The Hollow Walker is a zombie too. Cars: the auto box holds each gear instead of flicking to third in half a second, tyres keep their grip when they spin instead of doing endless burnouts, sharper steering at speed, the handbrake holds a parked car on slopes, and the speedo reads wheel speed. Roundabout grass is finer and matte. New Forge props: two-storey house, servo canopy, blown V8, 426 Hemi, 1979 pickup V8, oil cans, .45 revolver and scoped rifle. F9 reports now say what's under your crosshair and the state of the nearest car.

Two new guns you can find, pick up and fire: a scoped .308 hunting rifle (5-round bolt action, takes 7.62 rounds) and a .45 Magnum revolver (new .45 ammo); they turn up in military crates, ordinary crates and scav camps, and creative mode starts with both. Three new garage engines, each with its own Engine Simulator sound: a Ford 400 V8 out of a '79 pickup, a Chrysler 426 Hemi with its 4-speed, and a blown big-block with twin superchargers (with blower whine). Bridges: the ends of the decks now meet the road at the right height (most were sitting low, some stopped short), and the bridge sides and undersides are no longer drawn near-black. Gun pictures in the inventory now fill their space properly.

The whole map's roads rebuilt with the road generator from OpenStreetMap: proper junctions, roundabouts with kerbed islands, lane markings and the motorway (bridges keep their decks). Wollumbin / Mt Warning and the ranges round the map are now on the skyline, at their real heights; the haze is lighter so you can see them. Servo canopies on the real service stations and old two-storey houses along the streets. Scav camps laid out like someone lives there: a proper wall, seats round the fire, a store, a tip and a workshop. LAN multiplayer: Pause > Multiplayer to host or join a game on your network.

0.3 update, part 1: the world. Towns and farms are full of buildings now (about 20,000, made by a new house generator: Queenslanders, fibro cottages, brick houses, two-storeys, sheds, machinery sheds, dairies, workshops, warehouses), and you can walk into every one. Rooms are furnished for what they are and the cupboards, fridges, wardrobes and shelves have loot that fits the room; loot comes back if you stay away half an hour, and further from town the odd better find turns up. Doors open and close (F); zombies push them open. The Ampol servo is back at the real fuel stations, shop and workshop fitted out. Roads now lie flat on the ground (no more edges catching the wheels) and grass grips like grass. Day and night (an hour a day, 15 minutes of night, more zombies after dark), rain, storms with lightning, morning fog. The game saves itself: the host keeps the world, everyone keeps their own character.

Roads painted into the terrain (no more flicker or grass through the road). Grass density even around you. Step up lips and stairs (no bump at the bottom of Queenslander stairs). Zombies follow you through doorways and up stairs. Windows: open, climb through (Space), shoot out. Roller doors open/shut with F, zombies can't. Board up doors and windows with G (hammer, nails, planks); zombies bash through, pry off with F and a hammer. Pick up chairs, stools, crates and more (middle mouse). Binoculars and torch equip in primary/secondary with their own models; tape a torch to any gun, T toggles it. New loot: tape, hammer, nails, planks. Engine oil sits sideways in the bag. Project cars: rolling chassis and loose bodies at sheds and behind houses. Spanner + K opens the garage on the car in front of you. Car boots/trays hold stuff. Cars you drive are saved. Co-op: no friendly fire. Survival starts without a car. Fixed the invisible wall left by dead zombies.

Shops! Main streets are now rows of shopfronts after Murwillumbah's: tall parapets with the building's name and year (stepped, curved, pediment, flat or 60s box), awnings on tie rods over the footpath, highlight windows, big display windows on tiled stall boards, recessed entries, posted verandahs and balconies on the pubs. Chemists, hardware, grocers, cafes, newsagents, clothes and op shops, sports stores, pubs and banks, each with their own shelves and loot (bandages at the chemist, nails and planks at the hardware, ammo at the sports store, a safe in the bank). Some have a flat upstairs with its own street door. Shop windows can be shot out and climbed through. Shops face the main street, not the lane. Fixed the rail across the top of upstairs stairs. Note: the town layout changed, so cupboards and boarded-up doors start fresh.

The real valley: every house, shed, farmhouse and shop is now where it really is. Buildings come from the real map (OpenStreetMap plus building outlines traced from satellite photos), at their real size and angle, facing their street: about 36,000 of them, up from 21,000 mostly made-up ones. Farmhouses sit out on the farms with their sheds, hillside houses are up on stumps, tall houses are two storeys, backyard sheds are where they really are. Queenslander front stairs now always reach the ground: on a steep block they turn at a landing and run down along the verandah. Small garden sheds have a door instead of a roller door. Note: the town layout changed again, so cupboards and boarded-up doors start fresh.

Malls, part 1: Sunnyvale Mall in Mount Ruin (the real Sunnyside). Drive in under it from the street: the car park is the ground floor, with wrecks left in the bays and the loading dock out the back. Along the street front: cafes, a bank, the bottle shop and other shops, and the entry lobby where a ramp wide enough for four trolleys climbs, turns 180 degrees and comes up onto the first floor (or take the stairs in the core). Upstairs: the concourse under a skylight (watch the missing panes), a supermarket with aisles, checkouts, chillers and a stockroom, a big furniture and electrical store, shop units behind roller shutters with stockrooms, the food court and its kitchens, toilets, the security office. Mall props: trolleys you can push about, checkouts, planters with dead palms, benches, bins, ATMs, the directory board, kiosks, clothes racks, mannequins. And about two dozen of the dead wandering the place: clear them out and they stay gone a couple of hours. Note: the town layout changed slightly, so cupboards and boarded-up doors start fresh.

Fixed: invisible walls inside Sunnyvale Mall (and anywhere a zombie got blown apart) that stopped your shots. The gore copy of a zombie's model kept the model's hidden collision box. Zombies now all use the Meshy hollow walker.
Sunnyvale Mall: the first floor's ceilings are now 6.5 m high for a proper sense of scale, and the concourse has a polished cream floor that catches the skylight.
Sunnyvale Mall: polished cream floors right through: the lobby, street shops, shop units, supermarket, furniture store and food court.
Fixed: T (torch), G (board up) and K (work on car) did nothing and filled the log with errors on every key press. Keys added in updates weren't being registered.

Faster towns and malls: each room's shelves and fittings now draw as one piece (about a quarter of the draw calls in Sunnyvale), buildings load in closer, lighter windows. Sunnyvale gets the modern look: glass shopfronts with see-through grilles, stepped bulkheads with downlights, polished floor with dark inlay bands, hanging signs and banners, black ramp with glass sides, lower ceilings inside the shops.
Flats over the shops are a proper floor plan now: a passage runs from the top of the stairs past the stairwell to the lounge, and every room upstairs opens off it.

Sunnyvale rebuilt from the real centre's floor plans. Ground: shops along the street, a lobby wrapping round the ramp, the bottle shop, car park west, east and under the supermarket, lift and stairs on the west wall, loading dock. Upstairs: the mall runs in a C round the open ramp well under skylights, variety store and shops on the street side, toilets and shops down the west, furniture and electrical store on the east, and the supermarket across the whole south half.

The ocean is back (the sea sheet was sitting under the sea bed). Twin City: the big centre near the border, built from the real Tweed City's centre map on one level, 380 m long: two supermarkets, department and discount stores, the hi-fi store, a food court, about 40 shops down three malls, and a five-screen cinema with a lobby. Cupboards and boards start fresh with this update.

Crafting and base building, first cut. N opens the make menu: bandages, first aid kits, rope, nails, tin sheets, planks, torches, a small pack and all the ammo, from scrap, rags, wire, gunpowder and spent cases now found in sheds, hardware shops, wardrobes and gun shelves. M (with a hammer) is build mode: walls, doorways, window walls, half walls, floors and roofs, stairs and a storage crate, in wood, tin or brick. Wheel picks the piece, Tab the material, R turns it, [ and ] lower and raise it, left click builds, X pulls a piece down. Zombies can beat what you build down, and it is saved with the world.

Fighting and survival. Put the gun away (H) and the left button swings the best weapon you carry: fists, knife, tyre iron, pipe wrench, cricket bat, crowbar, machete, axe, sledgehammer (found in sheds, kitchens, hardware and sports shops; you start with a knife). Q kicks them off you, and a kick off a running jump sends them flying. Alt dodges, crouching at a sprint slides, and jumping at a wall or fence up to head height climbs it. X throws a brick, a bottle (they go and look), a petrol bomb (make it with N) or the weapon itself. Stamina, food and water bars: eat and drink or you slow down and starve. Zombies come in walkers, runners and brutes, scream to bring others, grab you, and are faster at night.

Cars as you find them. Family cars now sit in driveways and yards, each in its own state: worn or good engine, flat or charged battery, some fuel or none, and the key in the ignition, hidden in the cab, or gone. K beside a car opens under the bonnet: look it over, search for the key, try a key you have found in a house (one in three fits), or hotwire it with a length of wire (your odds rise with your mechanic level). Pouring in fuel, topping up oil and cleaning the plugs need no tools; repairing the engine and swapping batteries need a shifter. Cars burn fuel now, and a worn engine is slow and stalls. In creative every car just goes.

Thicker, more tropical bush: palms, figs, bananas and bamboo now grow through the forest and out in the open, bananas, bamboo and palms come in clumps, ferns in drifts, about twice the trees in open country and more along wet ground, the odd giant tree, and more scrub and understory everywhere. If the frame rate drops, lower plant density in the settings.

Fixes. Twin City: the ground under it is levelled so it no longer sits behind a wall, every mall now has a way in from outside (there were none), and every shop has a door. Weapons and anything else you drop show under on the ground near me straight away. Oracle mode: a World tab in the palette with fly speed in m/s, time of day and weather, and P drops the player wherever you look at any distance. Grass: no longer black (lit like the ground and toned to it) and sunk so it stops floating on slopes.

Kicked zombies now go down in a heap and tumble (a proper ragdoll), lie there a moment, then climb back to their feet and come at you again; a brick or a thrown weapon knocks them over too, and you can finish them on the ground. Brutes only stagger unless it is a flying kick. Your character's leg now kicks and the arm swings when you hit. New sky: drifting clouds that thicken with the weather, stars and a moon at night.

Greener ground: the open country and the forest floor were dry gold, now the green of the wet subtropics, and the grass on top is toned to match. Sugar cane: the cane paddocks from the map now grow standing cane, three metres tall in rows, out to about 200 m.

Towns re-laid. Houses are turned square to their street, sit clear of the road and clear of each other. Sheds are for farms and industrial land now; in town there is only the odd small garden shed down a back yard, and clusters of houses in the country are houses, not one farm and a row of sheds. About 2,700 fewer sheds. Every building was re-rolled for this, so houses look different and cupboards, boards and anything you built inside an old house start fresh.

Malls. The wall that boxed in Twin City is gone (the game was walling the whole block, not the building). Twin City now has its diagonal mall: a high glass-roofed court with two rows of shops standing at the real angle, and all mall roofs are higher. Bay Mall, the big centre at the north end by the border, is built from the real Tweed Mall floor plan: the long mall down the middle, three cross malls, three supermarkets, the big store on the east, about 45 shops and a food court. The land now carries on north of the old map edge for it to stand on.

The map now runs three kilometres further north, past the border: the real coastline and beaches, the real streets, about 2,400 buildings where the real ones stand, and Bay Mall moved to where Tweed Mall really is on Wharf Street. New building: beachfront towers of five to fourteen storeys with a foyer you can walk into and a lift (F at the panel in the car) to one floor part-way up and to the roof. The ground up there is from public elevation data for now, not the lidar.

The town's buildings, where OpenStreetMap says the real ones are: schools (rows of classrooms off a corridor), churches, hospitals and clinics (wards, a dispensary), police stations (cells, an armoury), fire stations (engine bay with roller doors, bunks), post offices, motels (a row of rooms each with its own door), halls and clubs, and stand-alone pubs, each with its name over the door and its own furniture and loot. Ten more kinds of plant under the trees and along the edges. Buildings were re-rolled again for this, so cupboards and boards start fresh.

The ground north of the old map edge now comes from your lidar wherever it has data (the New South Wales side, about 60 percent of the new strip); across the border it stays on public elevation data, matched and blended in. Bay Mall has its multi-level car park: three open concrete decks with ramps you can drive up. Buildings up north were re-placed on the new ground.

Fixes and Forge tools. The country north of the old map edge now actually arrives: its ground and roads were never in the updates before, so it should finally meet the rest of the valley, with bush, grass and real beaches instead of bare lawn. Zombies follow you into houses: through the doors, round to the back door, up the stairs. Houses no longer sit on the roads (about 1,000 small buildings that couldn't be moved clear are gone, so cupboards start fresh). Twin City and Bay Mall have their entrances back. Slower clouds. In Forge: a Time & Weather tab (time, stop the clock, weather and fog sliders) and a Map tab, click anywhere to teleport.

Proper melee animations. Kicks, punches and weapon swings are now real motion-captured moves instead of a bent leg and arm: a thrust kick and a flying kick (the boot lands a beat after you press it), jabs and hooks, one-handed swings for the tyre iron, crowbar, wrench and machete, two-handed swings for the bat, axe and sledge, stabs for the knife, and the weapon sits in your hand. Zombies flinch when you hit them, stumble back when you boot them, and climb back to their feet instead of tilting up like a plank. The kick is a shove now, not a cannon: only the flying kick floors them. Hillside houses sit lower on the high side so their steps reach the ground, and about 460 houses perched on cliffs are gone (cupboards start fresh once more).

Twin City rebuilt from the real centre's directory plan. Every shop and anchor is traced from the plan, so the walls stand on their real angles: the diagonal mall runs corner to corner, both west wings curve away to the south-west, and the big stores are where they really are (HOLLIS & CRANE up north-west, FRESHWAY north-east, GREENGATE and BIG VALUE down south, REGENT CINEMAS and VOLT ELECTRICAL on the west side). 114 shops, 16 ways in, a glass roof on a frame over the malls, shop names over the fronts. New and rough: zombies inside it only walk straight at you, and the malls themselves are bare (no benches or kiosks yet).

Twin City built from your colour-keyed plan. Walls and shop fronts where you drew them, 12 ways in, 4 toilet blocks, covered walkways with posts round the outside shops. Three travelators go down to an underground car park under the whole centre (lit, columns, bay lines), and a car ramp comes down through the cinema building. Stairs inside the mall go up to the REGENT CINEMAS lobby and three cinemas with raked seats. Still rough: zombies inside walk straight at you, and the mall floor has no benches or kiosks yet.

full.notes: First Godot build with the launcher built in. Pause menu with graphics settings, Forge mode with phys gun and terrain sculpting, 27 drivable bodies, 52 props, your survivor as a full body, cab view and hop-out fixes.
